items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: But anyhow, Miss Tate wrote and told me that she wasn't any too optimistic about the job.

ctx.x: Well, she, you see, she told me that they had been very busy. Mm-hmm. And he had tried to get the band out there before George left, but I don't know, there was some misunderstanding between, with Miss Tate, I don't know what happened. But anyhow, Miss Tate wrote and told me that she wasn't any too optimistic about the job. Now, I don't know what the terms was about. So, I said, well, that's just a dead issue until they come back. So, I know, I'm more than sure when they come back why something will be worked out…
Sure, they'd like to have the whole band.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: Well, Joe Rovershow, Howard, Jim, Miss Tate, George, they all left by plane.

ctx.x: Yeah, then you went back to Denmark.

Then we went back to Denmark and we left from there and went to Baden-Baden, Germany for a week for a TV show. So, naturally, it was more of a cabaret scene. And we rehearsed that whole week. And when we finished there, we left and went back to London. And that was when, well, everything was over with. Then the boys got ready to come on. Well, Joe Rovershow, Howard, Jim, Miss Tate, George, they all left by plane. Well, Jack and I came back by boat. And that was when we run into that 80-mile gale. And I'm telling…
